items.item_text: resume

Must possess valid California Driver's License to drive a County or University vehicle. Ability and means to travel on a flexible schedule as needed, proof of liability damage insurance on vehicle used is required. Reimbursement of job-related travel will be reimbursed according to University policies.
Statewide Program Leadership, Design, and Management
Design, conduct, manage, and evaluate statewide and multi-county education and technical assistance programs supporting the adoption of science-based climate smart farming and ranching practices.
Serve as a subject matter expert for UC ANR’s Climate Smart Agriculture technical assistance programs supporting Climate Bond–funded HSP and SWEEP block grants.

Use technical expertise and program management concepts to analyze, develop, and deliver statewide training curriculum, guidance materials, and standardized technical assistance packages for state, local, and regional climate smart agriculture programs.

Identify and facilitate collaboration opportunities with partners, preparing action and implementation plans, and designing evaluation plans to measure local and regional outcomes and impacts of climate smart agriculture projects.

Exercise autonomy in formulating program strategies, designing processes, and addressing complex issues related to climate adaptation, resilience, and the equitable distribution of CDFA funding resources statewide.

Provide technical expertise and training on specialized topics such as soil health, irrigation efficiency, rangeland management, manure management, greenhouse gas mitigation, and climate change adaptation.
Technical Assistance to Block Grant Recipients and Partners
Provide consultation to eligible organizations applying for Climate Bond–funded HSP and SWEEP block grants, as well as other state, local, or federally funded climate smart agriculture programs.

Co-develop grant applications and scopes of work with partners, outlining UC ANR’s role in extending technical assistance capacity, developing curriculum and training materials, and ensuring the delivery of direct and meaningful benefits to underserved and priority populations.

Support block grant recipients and other funded partners in administration of awarded projects, including planning, logistics, development of outreach strategies, refinement of project selection processes, and coordination of technical assistance delivery.

Lead or contribute to the development of curriculum, guidance documents, and training resources for technical assistance programs such as CDFA’s Alternative Manure Management Program and Dairy Plus Program, dairy sustainability initiatives, sustainable rangeland management projects, and related climate smart agriculture efforts.

Train block grant recipients, partner organizations, technical assistance providers on quantification tools, practice standards, reporting requirements, and implementation strategies associated with climate smart agriculture adoption. Partner training may require travel outside of specified county regions.
Extension, Outreach, and Technical Assistance to Producers

Lead outreach, education, and technical assistance activities that promote climate smart agriculture practices, including soil health, manure management, and irrigation efficiency, to mitigate greenhouse gas emissions and adapt to climate change impacts.

Serve as a subject-matter lead for climate smart agriculture initiatives, directing high-level technical assistance, cross-disciplinary teams, and stakeholder engagement. Manage projects such as sustainable rangeland health grants, strategic economic case studies on CSA adoption, and advanced management training courses.

Provide regional and statewide technical assistance to producers including DACs, SDACs, SDFRs, Tribes, and other vulnerable populations including supporting project consultation, design, application, implementation, verification, and outcome reporting.
Coordinate and conduct multilingual outreach activities through site visits, workshops, webinars, field days, train-the-trainer events, and one-on-one project consultations or site visits.
Support producers with soil sampling, vendor coordination, project modifications, invoicing, advance payment requests, and documentation required by BGRs and CDFA.
Facilitate connections between producers and UC Cooperative Extension Advisors, researchers, technical service providers, and partner organizations.
Data Analysis, Evaluation, and Reporting
Independently gather, analyze, and synthesize data to evaluate progress toward achieving program goals and objectives.

Identify opportunities to improve program effectiveness and provide data-driven recommendations to the Climate Smart Agriculture Program leadership team, CDFA expert panels, and other partner or community forums.
Develop and contribute to program evaluations including impact reports and case studies documenting producer, community, and ecosystem benefits of implemented practices.
Maintain enrollment data, educational curriculum, and documentation required for grant management, audits, and program evaluation.
Synthesize scientific, policy, and programmatic information to support internal decision-making and external reporting to CDFA and other partners
Bachelor’s degree in agricultural sciences, environmental sciences, natural resources, social sciences, or a related field, and/or equivalent combination of education and experience.
Advanced knowledge of climate smart agriculture practices, including soil health, irrigation efficiency, manure management, greenhouse gas mitigation, and climate adaptation strategies.
Advanced knowledge of CDFA climate smart agriculture financial incentive programs, block grants, and Climate Bond priorities.
In-depth experience in community education, outreach, and technical assistance with agricultural producers.
Strong written, verbal, and interpersonal communication skills, including experience communicating technical information to diverse audiences and partners.
Ability to work independently, exercise sound judgment, and manage multiple priorities simultaneously.
Post-baccalaureate coursework or degrees related to agriculture, sustainability, climate change, water resources, or public policy.
Experience working with disadvantaged or underserved farming communities, including SDFRs and Tribes.
Bilingual proficiency (Spanish/English or other languages commonly spoken by California agricultural producers).
Experience with state or federal grant-funded programs and reporting requirements.
Special Conditions of Employment:
Travel to farms, partner organizations, and other sites within assigned regions and statewide, including occasional evening or weekend work.

As of January 1, 2014, ANR is a smoke- and tobacco-free environment in which smoking, the use of smokeless tobacco products, and the use of unregulated nicotine products (e-cigarettes), is strictly prohibited.

“Misconduct” means any violation of the policies governing employee conduct at the applicant’s previous place of employment, including, but not limited to, violations of policies prohibiting sexual harassment, sexual assault, or other forms of harassment, or discrimination, as defined by the employer. For reference, below are UC’s policies addressing some forms of misconduct:
UC Sexual Violence and Sexual Harassment Policy
UC Anti-Discrimination Policy
Abusive Conduct in the Workplace
It is the policy of the University of California to undertake affirmative action and anti-discrimination efforts, consistent with its obligations as a Federal and State contractor.

The University reserves the right to make employment contingent upon successful completion of the background check. This is a designated position requiring a background check and may require fingerprinting due to the nature of the job responsibilities. UC ANR does hire people with conviction histories and reviews information received in the context of the job responsibilities.

As a condition of employment, you will be required to comply with the University of California Policy on Vaccination Programs, as may be amended or revised from time to time.  Federal, state, or local public health directives may impose additional requirements.

Misconduct Disclosure Requirement: As a condition of employment, the final candidate who accepts an offer of employment will be required to disclose if they have been subject to any final administrative or judicial decisions within the last seven years determining that they committed any misconduct; or have filed an appeal of a finding of substantiated misconduct with a previous employer.
